0.0.n: Part of the venue name エンゼルスタジアム, Angel Stadium.

0.1.n: A borrowed English word forming the second part of the venue name.

0.2.n: Marks the location where the event takes place.

1.0.n: The name of the event, written in katakana.

1.1.n: Identifies the event as what was held.

1.2.n: 開催され is a connecting form of 開催される, the passive of 開催する; the sentence continues.

2.0.n: The name of the baseball team, distinct from エンゼル in the stadium name.

2.1.n: Sets the team as the context in which he was the first Japanese player.

2.2.n: 日本人 means Japanese person; 初 adds the idea of being the first.

2.3.n: Connects 日本人初 to 選手, describing what kind of player he was.

2.4.n: Refers to a baseball player here; it can also refer to athletes in other sports.

2.5.n: Marks the resulting role with なる; となる sounds more formal than になる.

2.6.n: Past form of なる; the whole phrase describes the person named next.

3.0.n: This is his family name; Japanese names normally put the family name first.

3.1.n: This character belongs to the given name 滋利; the subtitle splits the name across word tokens.

3.2.n: 利 completes the given name 滋利, and 氏 is a formal title commonly used in news.

3.3.n: Marks Hasegawa as the person who was invited and interviewed.

3.4.n: 招待され is a connecting form of 招待される, the passive of 招待する.

3.5.n: A borrowed English word used with 受ける for being interviewed.

3.6.n: Marks インタビュー as what he received.

3.7.n: Connecting form of 受ける; インタビューを受ける means to be interviewed.

4.0.n: 後 attaches to 引退 to indicate the period following retirement.

4.1.n: Connects 引退後 to 生活, specifying which period of his life is meant.

4.2.n: Refers to his everyday life following retirement.

4.3.n: Lists topics without implying these are the only ones he discussed.

4.4.n: Refers to golf, which developed beyond a leisure activity.

4.5.n: Marks 趣味 as what grew more intense.

4.6.n: て-form of 高じる, linking his deepening hobby to the result of becoming a professional.

5.0.n: Short for プロフェッショナル; combines with ゴルファー to describe his status.

5.1.n: A borrowed English word; together with プロ it names his new role.

5.2.n: Marks the role he came to have in the expression となる.

5.3.n: Past form of なる, describing a change that had already happened.

5.4.n: Turns the preceding statement about becoming a professional golfer into a topic he can discuss.

5.5.n: Indicates that the listed topics are examples, not a complete list.

5.6.n: Marks the listed topics as what he talked about.

5.7.n: Describes English as something he handles well.

5.8.n: Links 得意 to 英語, describing English as a language he is good at.

5.9.n: Names the language he used for the interview.

5.10.n: Marks the language used to communicate.

5.11.n: 話す in て-form plus いました gives a polite description of an ongoing past action.

0.tip: で marks where an action or event happens.

1.lit: Japanese Heritage Night was held, and
1.tip: 開催され leaves the sentence open, linking this event to what follows.

2.lit: Who became the first Japanese player for the Angels,
2.tip: This entire phrase describes Hasegawa, whose name comes in the next line.

3.lit: Mr. Shigetoshi Hasegawa was invited and received an interview, and
3.tip: インタビューを受ける literally means to receive an interview, but naturally means to be interviewed.

4.lit: Life after retirement and his hobby growing more intense,
4.tip: や links post-retirement life with the longer topic about his hobby leading to professional golf.

5.lit: He was discussing becoming a professional golfer, among other things, in English, which he is good at.
5.tip: こと turns the preceding description of becoming a professional golfer into a noun-like topic for 話す.
